claims.text: The proposed alloy has composition Ti40Ni40Cr10Al10, with Ti and Ni as the primary constituents.
Conventionally cast Ti40Ni40Cr10Al10 has a relatively coarse, equilibrium microstructure.
The intervention uses melt-spinning at a cooling rate greater than 10^5 K/s.
Melt-spinning is followed by annealing at 700°C for 15 minutes in an inert atmosphere.
Rapid solidification produces a metastable, nanocrystalline, supersaturated phase mixture in Ti40Ni40Cr10Al10.
Subsequent annealing promotes formation of a controlled, uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitate distribution.
Severe undercooling creates a high grain-boundary density and a nonequilibrium nanostructure.
The annealing-generated nanoscale precipitates pin dislocations.
The annealing-generated nanoscale precipitates pin grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary strengthening and precipitation hardening increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
Grain-boundary strengthening and precipitation hardening improve elevated-temperature creep resistance.
The processed alloy will have statistically significantly higher yield strength than the conventionally cast alloy at approximately 800–900°C.
The processed alloy will have a lower creep rate than the conventionally cast alloy at approximately 800–900°C.
The expected relative mechanical-property improvement is at least approximately 10–20%.
The beneficial effects can persist up to approximately 800–900°C if rapid coarsening does not occur.
Long-term thermal stability of the nanostructured and precipitate-controlled microstructure is uncertain.
Less than a 10% improvement in yield strength or creep rate relative to the cast control, or rapid microstructural coarsening, is specified as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly characterized as a high-entropy alloy subject to the query's definition, but Ti40Ni40Cr10Al10 contains only four elements and has Ti and Ni at 40 at% each. It therefore violates both the requirement of at least five elements and the stated 5–35 at% range.
